A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mean-estimation work, retaining FastGD, MinSumSelect, and the sample-complexity lower bounds. All pages, figures, equations, and sections referenced as appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports algorithms, mathematical proofs, and constructed lower-bound instances, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v4 Section 8 reports original accuracy and runtime experiments on three real datasets and synthetic Gaussian data, including repeated-run results.

M1.justification: v4 introduces the coordinate-wise median as a standalone final aggregation procedure; in v3 it only initializes FastGD. This substantially expands the proposed estimator choices. FastGD's projection-and-median updates and MinSumSelect remain essentially unchanged; the improved FastGD runtime guarantee primarily comes from stronger analysis.

E1.justification: v3 contains no empirical dataset coverage. v4 adds mean-estimation evaluations on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CoverType, and synthetic multivariate Gaussian data. The image datasets are used as point sets for mean estimation, not classification.

E2.justification: v4 newly evaluates CSS, from Cohen-Addad, Saulpic, and Schwiegelshohn, and WY, from Woodruff and Yasuda, against the proposed estimators. It also includes the empirical mean in accuracy comparisons. v3 discusses these approaches theoretically but reports no corresponding empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 8 introduces uniform-subsampling evaluations using Alg/Opt and runtime, with real-data sample sizes from 10 to 10,000. New Gaussian experiments extend sample sizes to 500,000 in 200 dimensions and vary dimension from 10 to 1,000 with 10,000 points. These are new protocols, not revisions or reruns of v3 experiments.

E4.justification: v4 compares FastGD against its coordinate-median initialization to test whether gradient refinement helps. It also adds empirical sample-size and dimensionality sensitivity analyses, including large-sample runtime scaling. v3 has no corresponding empirical analyses; Figure 5 merely redisplays existing v4 accuracy results.

E5.justification: v4 Section 8.2.1 introduces 50 executions per algorithm and listed sample size, reporting averages and variances for the real-data comparisons, whose plots include shaded bands. v3 has no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. This does not establish additional runs for any pre-existing experiment.

E6.justification: v4 adds all measured cost-ratio and runtime results in Section 8. For example, Figure 2 shows CSS near Alg/Opt = 1 and FastGD slightly more accurate than CoordWiseMedian on MNIST; Figures 6–7 add Gaussian scaling results. These are newly reported outcomes, with no measured v3 counterparts.

T1.justification: v4 Theorem 3.1 replaces v3 Lemma 3.5's b log(1/δ) r initialization bound with sqrt(5) r, enabling the constant-iteration FastGD guarantee in Theorem 4.1. It also adds the covariance-trace convergence bound in Theorem 3.2, estimator-comparison arguments in Proposition 3.3, and a FastGD nonconvergence counterexample. The earlier lower bounds and unit-ball generalization result are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand from two nearly optimal-time algorithms to three estimator choices, claiming optimal runtime for coordinate-median aggregation and FastGD. They add improved distributional convergence guarantees and a practical claim that the geometric-median-based approach is typically most competitive. The optimal sample-complexity claim remains.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains that FastGD need not converge to the geometric median. It adds interpretations of gradient refinement, preprocessing overhead, and why the empirical mean can perform well on benign distributions despite poor worst-case guarantees. It also reports the RAM limitation preventing larger synthetic experiments and discusses practical estimator tradeoffs absent from v3.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-and-results repository link, identifies the Google Colab default CPU, and discloses NumPy vectorization in discussing runtime behavior. These are useful but limited reproducibility disclosures beyond v3's pseudocode and theoretical constants; the linked resources themselves are not verified by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning through new discussions of data-dependent mean estimation and coresets, and relates its coordinate-median bound to earlier analyses including Minsker. It adds works such as Dang et al. and Catoni, and updates the cited best-known k-means learning rate using Cohen-Addad, Lattanzi, and Schwiegelshohn's 2025 work.

P1.justification: The abstract and contributions are rewritten around three estimators. The initialization topic becomes a central coordinate-median section, the good-sample probabilistic lemma moves to preliminaries, and the former generalization discussion becomes a separate section. Retained proof exposition is reorganized, although unfinished cross-references such as 'Appendix ??' remain.

P2.justification: The two-column v3 layout becomes a single-column manuscript. The geometric illustration in Figure 1 is retained and relocated, while Table 1 and Figures 2–7 add dataset summaries and multiple accuracy/runtime displays. Figure 5 specifically replots the real-data accuracy curves on a linear sample-size axis.

improvement.justification: The new coordinate-median proof turns v3's initialization step into a complete optimal-time estimator and removes FastGD's extra iteration factor, substantially simplifying and strengthening the central result. The experiments add useful practical characterization and repeated-run reporting. These gains outweigh localized defects: Proposition 3.3(1) claims exact recovery although its proof places the coordinate median at the origin and the true mean elsewhere, and the abstract's practical preference is not fully aligned with Section 8.2's recommendations.
